newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Germany says Cambodia aid depends on deforestation.
newsitem.headline: Germany says Cambodia aid depends on deforestation.

text.p: Germany has told Cambodia to curb deforestation or risk cuts in aid, and voiced concern about corruption and drug trafficking, a visiting German minister said on Friday.

German Minister for Economic Cooperation and Development Carl-Dieter Spranger said he had discussed the three problems in talks with Cambodian officials, including First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, since arriving on Wednesday.
Spranger said he had reiterated that Germany could no longer continue to provide substantial aid towards Cambodia's economic development if logging, both illegal and legal, continued.

"In all of the meetings, people recognised and assured me that the maintenance of forests and reforestation was a task of fundamental importance," he said, adding they were aware that action was a prerequisite to continued overseas cooperation.

"I did find there is a willingness to address the issues head on, for example there is the ban," Spranger said, referring to a December 31 government ban on log exports. "We will have to wait and see what happens in practice."

Pressure grew on Cambodia to review forestry policies after the International Monetary Fund last year scrapped a $20 million loan because of a lack of transparency in the government's accounting for logging revenues.
Spranger did not say what deforestation limit Germany would accept before cutting aid. He said the country would make its decision independently of other countries and financial institutions.
Germany had pledged more than 290 million marks in official development aid to Cambodia between 1992 and 1996, and agreed to give another 10 million in financial aid during Spranger's visit.
